The repaired definition restricts the field to R or C before all formulas; focused rendering and the Step-8 guard pass.

Both escalations were valid: the former application neither established that det^{-1}(1) was nonempty nor licensed its codimension-one conclusion. ETH differential-geometry notes independently confirm the determinant differential and dimension n^2-1.

The fatal reviews correctly found that the earlier refutation supplied no concrete large category and did not establish the size obstruction. The current proof cites that Set is large, constructs its identity monad directly from the standard endofunctor/unit/multiplication definition, and invokes the library size convention that [Set,Set] is not formed. The original bare phrase was convention-dependent and the prior proof supplied no lax-but-not-strong witness. The repaired claim is explicitly about lax monoidal functors and constructs the covariant power-set functor on cartesian Set; its comparison map sends (A,B) to A×B, satisfies coherence, and misses the diagonal subset of {0,1}×{0,1}. MIT sources confirm that strong means lax with invertible comparison maps, so this witness refutes the revised universal claim.

The reviewers correctly found that the former local fact omitted absolute continuity and the precise Radon-Nikodym hypotheses. The repaired proof first shows the x^{-1/2} density has finite mass 2, derives nu << lambda from null-set integration, and supplies the common finite exhaustion [-n,n] for the sigma-finite base before identifying the derivative. That derivative is unbounded near zero, so the false claim is rigorously refuted.

The prior reviews correctly found that positivity of lambda((0,1]) was not licensed by the cited identity alone. The repair adds the Lebesgue-Stieltjes interval-increment theorem, yielding lambda((0,1])=1. The Cantor component gives positive mass to a lambda-null set, excluding absolute continuity, while the Lebesgue component gives mass outside every lambda-null concentration set, excluding singularity. Thus the finite sum measure is a valid counterexample.

The prior facts did not license the absolute-continuity implication. The repair now cites the null-set integral theorem together with the exact definition of nu << lambda: the x^{-1} density measure vanishes on every lambda-null set. Yet for epsilon=1 every delta fails on (0,delta/2), whose lambda measure is below delta while the density integral is infinite. This positive, hence signed, sigma-finite but nonfinite measure proves finiteness is essential.

This adjudication also repaired a residual provenance gap by citing the Lebesgue-Stieltjes identity and interval formula for lambda((0,1])=1; Hunter Example 6.28 confirms this exact counterexample.

The repaired converse explicitly chooses the first configurations whose stacks are Yalpha and alpha. Before each first exposure the run cannot inspect the protected suffix, so both transition segments lift to every suffix beta and satisfy the exact [p,Z,r] definition. Standard university PDA-to-CFG notes use this same suffix-preserving fragment semantics.

The escalations were valid: the original proof lacked an SVD/pseudoinverse construction citation and did not restrict the scalar field. The repaired statement and Given explicitly take F in {R,C}; [L4] supplies the SVD, full column rank makes every column singular value positive, and direct multiplication shows (A* A)^{-1}A* satisfies all four Penrose equations, so uniqueness identifies it with A+. Cornell and Stanford notes independently give this exact formula.

Both fatal findings are repaired. The current proof cites the real/complex spectral theorem to establish Hermitian diagonalizability before applying power iteration. It also correctly writes alpha_k r_k, not r_k, after phase rotation and uses |alpha_k|=1 for the norm. Orthogonal invariance cancels the Rayleigh cross terms, giving quadratic eigenvalue error and linear residual error; Cornell notes independently confirm Hermitian Rayleigh error is second order in eigenvector error.

The converse uses |nu_a|(X)=integral |dnu_a/dmu|, consistent with Hunter.

Their singular-vector image spaces are im A and im A*, so the self-adjoint-idempotent criterion yields the stated orthogonal projections, consistent with Stanford CS205L.

The first fatal review correctly found that addition of unrestricted infinite signed measures can be undefined; the repaired theorem restricts to finite signed or finite complex measures, so the sum is well-defined. The second review correctly found complex uniqueness uncited; L2 now cites the finite-complex density corollary as well as signed uniqueness. Linearity of the integral makes h1+h2 a representing density, and uniqueness yields the result, consistent with university measure-theory treatments of Radon–Nikodym additivity.

Both fatal reviews correctly identified a missing smoothness upgrade in the earlier proof. The repaired step 2.1 now applies higher regularity to the explicit source map: because the original coordinate representative is smooth, the same map is C^k for every finite k, and uniqueness of its local inverse gives one inverse of every finite regularity, hence a smooth inverse. The target shear and its explicit inverse are smooth, so their composites are smooth charts. This is the standard constant-rank construction in Lee and Merry.

For n at least 3, trailing Householder similarities preserve earlier zeros, and symmetry turns upper Hessenberg form into tridiagonal form, matching MIT and Cornell numerical-analysis notes.

This matches the classical constant-rank continuity result and the Stanford zero-singular-value example.
